correctness.rationale: Retaining exactly one oriented two-letter word per edge and killing all words of length three or more makes the stated basis a monomial quotient. Any product of three nonunits is zero, and their span is a nilpotent two-sided ideal with field quotient, hence the Jacobson radical. Squaring in that ideal gives one coefficient c_i c_j per edge, never 2c_i c_j, and leaves all m edge coordinates free. The resulting edge ideal equals the intersection of coordinate primes obtained by setting c_i=0 outside maximal independent sets: a monomial avoids the edge ideal exactly when its support lies in some such set. This proves reducedness over every field and identifies the components and their dimensions. In the whole algebra the scalar equation is lambda²=0, so the radical contains lambda; modulo lambda the ideal is the same reduced edge ideal. The independent-support strata have affine-times-torus class and point counts as stated, while the monomials of exact support S contribute (t/(1−t))^|S|, with an extra free factor (1−t)^(-m). Over F2, the explicit table is polynomial size, and division of the full or radical count by 2^m recovers the independent-set count; the conclusion is Turing hardness, not parsimony. In characteristic two over an algebraically closed field, commutativity makes every square-coordinate equation a square of a linear form, proving the reduced-linearity obstruction. An edge forces two distinct maximal independent sets, so its locus is reducible.

value.rationale: This is a uniform link between two natural structures, not a recomputation of graph enumerators: even a cube-zero radical in a short monomial algebra can have arbitrary graph independence-complex component patterns in its squaring locus. The characteristic-two contrast explains why order of multiplication matters, and the explicit sparse multiplication rule yields a hardness transfer in a restricted finite-field class. The standard formulas for edge ideals become geometric and computational information about the chosen algebra after the realization.
residual_risks: No classification up to algebra isomorphism, universal statement about commutative algebras outside the stated characteristic, or complexity claim stronger than the exact counting reduction.
